chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamza Al-Thumali, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: There will be tribulation until the seventieth [year]. And he used to say: After the tribulation, there will be ease/peace. But the seventy years have passed and we have not seen ease!

So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: O Thabit, indeed Allah the Exalted had fixed this matter [the end of tribulation] at seventy. But when Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was martyred, the anger of Allah intensified upon the people of the earth, so He postponed it to one hundred and forty years. We informed you, but you publicized the hadith and revealed the veil of the secret, so Allah postponed it further and did not fix a specific time for it with us after that.
Allah erases what He wills and confirms [what He wills], and with Him is the Mother of the Book.
Abu Hamza said: And I said that to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said: That was indeed the case.

key_terms.أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ: The Mother of the Book (Quran), referring to the divine source of decree

ai.seo_question: Why did the time for the end of tribulation change from 70 to 140 years according to Imam Al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the dynamic nature of the Imam's reappearance timeline, linking the initial seventy-year period to the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (a.s) as a catalyst for divine wrath that extended the wait to 140 years. The subsequent delay, attributed to the narrator Abu Hamza al-Thumali publicizing the secret, underscores the Shia concept of *taqiyya* and the fluidity of eschatological signs. The reference to Surah Ar-Ra'd illustrates how divine decree is not static but responsive to human actions and divine wisdom.
